impact.title: Same budget, <accent>different</accent> curve.
impact.desc: Website, custom software, automation or AI — whichever you commission, the work proves its worth in month twelve, not on handover day. These six lines show where a well-built system ends up over time.
impact.note: Indicative model — it illustrates the typical effect of technology and setup choices over time. It is not measured client data and not a guarantee. Real outcomes vary with sector, scope and how your processes are structured.

automation.label: Process automation
automation.head: Less work done by hand
automation.detail: Repeating work — preparing quotes, entering data, assembling reports — moves into workflows. The figure is the hours a single process takes from your team each month. Once automation is in place those hours do not come back; the system keeps running without you.

ai.label: Capacity through AI
ai.head: Most requests handled automatically
ai.detail: AI assistants and agents handle the routine share of incoming requests end to end; the team only deals with exceptions. The figure is the proportion of requests resolved without a human touching them. This is how volume grows without new headcount.

performance.label: System performance
performance.head: A system that doesn't slow down
performance.detail: Whether it is a brochure site or custom software, we build to a performance budget. A system that accumulates plugins and layers gets heavier with every feature; one built with measurement holds its response time steady as scope grows.

visibility.label: Search & AI visibility
visibility.head: SEO built in, not bolted on
visibility.detail: Technical SEO, structured data and multilingual hreflang are in place before launch, and content is structured so AI models can read and cite it. Index 100 = visibility on launch day.

conversion.label: Enquiry conversion
conversion.head: Same traffic, more enquiries
conversion.detail: Forms, calls and flows are measured, and what is measured gets improved. The difference comes not from more visitors but from a larger share of the same visitors turning into real enquiries — without touching the ad budget.

maintenance.label: Maintenance load
maintenance.head: Infrastructure that needs no tending
maintenance.detail: The monthly time spent keeping the system alive. On setups that rely on a plugin ecosystem and manual intervention this line grows every month; with version control, automated tests and managed infrastructure it shrinks.

gel-gez-gor.title: Gel Gez Gor
gel-gez-gor.summary: Trend detection, WhatsApp notifications and social content automation for the Gel Gez Gor classifieds site.
body: We built an automation layer for Gel Gez Gor, a classifieds site in North Cyprus, that detects trending listings automatically. The platform itself belongs to the client; our work was the pipeline that reads featured listings from the site and notifies listing owners via WhatsApp.

The same system generates a ready-to-post social media visual and an AI-assisted caption for each listing and can publish them to Instagram and Facebook. The team now runs the monitoring and posting work it used to do by hand from a single panel.

caseStudy.challenge: At Gel Gez Gor, manually tracking trending listings, reaching out to listing owners one by one, and preparing a separate social media graphic for every listing took time and produced inconsistent results. The platform itself had no API for trend detection. What was needed was an automation layer that could detect trending listings straight from the site's own HTML structure, notify listing owners over WhatsApp, and generate a ready-made Instagram/Facebook graphic and caption for each listing — one that wouldn't break easily if the site's structure changed, and that would run on its own several times a day.
caseStudy.solution: The pipeline reads gelgezgor.com's static HTML with Cheerio to extract trending listing cards; results are saved locally to SQLite/Drizzle, or directly to a cloud PostgreSQL database in the Vercel environment, then enriched from the detail page. Listing owners get automatic notifications via the Twilio WhatsApp Business API, with a separate client already in place for migrating to Meta's own WhatsApp Cloud API. On the social side, a Sharp-based SVG-overlay-and-image-composite approach produces six graphic templates across three themes (Modern, Elegant, Bold) times two variants (dark/light); template choice auto-rotates based on the listing's title and category. Captions and hashtags are generated first with Gemini, with an automatic fallback to template-based text if the API call fails; an optional AI-generated background via Imagen 3 is also attempted, again falling back to the template. Generated graphics can be published directly to Instagram (single post and carousel) and Facebook through the Meta Graph API. All of this comes together in a single orchestrator triggered twice a day by node-cron; an Express-based panel provides manual triggering and status tracking, with a dry-run mode for testing without touching production.
highlights: A Cheerio-based scraper with documented selectors reads trending listing cards straight from the site's static HTML — no headless browser required.
Automatic listing-owner notifications via the Twilio WhatsApp Business API, with a separate client already in place for migrating to the Meta WhatsApp Cloud API.
A Sharp-based graphics engine auto-rotates between six templates (3 themes × 2 variants) based on listing category.
Caption and hashtag generation with Gemini, backed by an automatic fallback chain to template-based text on failure.
Generated graphics publish directly to Instagram (single post and carousel) and Facebook through the Meta Graph API, with a dry-run mode for safe testing before going live.
caseStudy.outcome: The result is a pipeline that unifies trend detection for Gel Gez Gor into a single automated flow, from scraping through WhatsApp notification to social media publishing. Manual control and a dry-run mode in the panel allow safe testing before going live. The system was built to be portable, running equally well on SQLite on a single machine or on cloud PostgreSQL on Vercel.

nexos-investment.title: Nexos Investment
nexos-investment.summary: Custom real estate listing & management system built from scratch — maps, i18n, automated PDF/PPT proposals.
body: Off-the-shelf themes couldn't meet Nexos Investment's needs (advanced listing management, map-based display, multi-language, automated proposal generation). We built a scalable listing management system from scratch with Next.js, PostgreSQL and Vercel: an interactive Google Maps + Leaflet clustered map, multi-language via next-intl, and automated PDF/PowerPoint proposal generation from listing data.

An admin panel with TipTap editing and drag-and-drop, PWA/offline support, Zod validation, Upstash rate-limiting and Playwright E2E tests delivered a production-grade platform. The firm now runs maps, proposals and content from one fully-controlled system — the technical peak of our portfolio.

caseStudy.challenge: Nexos Investment, a real estate investment firm managing many projects and listings in North Cyprus, was working with off-the-shelf real estate themes. Those themes couldn't support map-based, location-driven presentation, multilingual content (most investors are foreign), or generating an instant proposal document from listing data. Consultants had to build a presentation by hand for every proposal and manage listings separately in each language. The firm wanted a single platform, shaped around its own workflow, that would bring all of these processes together in one system.
caseStudy.solution: We built a real estate management system from scratch on Next.js 16 and PostgreSQL. On the public side, it covers listing/project browsing, filtering, a clustered interactive map on Google Maps and Leaflet (react-leaflet-cluster), and a 5-language (tr/en/ru/de/fa) content structure via next-intl. For consultants, we built a full admin panel with a TipTap rich-text editor and a drag-and-drop interface, managing listings, projects, sub-listings and floor plans. The presentation module instantly turns selected listing/project data into a PDF or PowerPoint proposal file using jsPDF and pptxgenjs, via html2canvas image capture. The system also runs as a PWA, with service-worker caching and offline page support. Input validation runs on Zod, abuse protection on Upstash rate-limiting, and critical flows are covered by Playwright E2E tests.
highlights: Interactive map: a clustered Leaflet map via react-leaflet-cluster plus Google Maps integration shows listing and project locations grouped on one screen.
Automated proposal generation: the presentation module instantly builds a PDF or PowerPoint proposal from listing data using pptxgenjs and jsPDF.
5-language structure: Turkish, English, Russian, German and Persian content managed via next-intl with per-language translation files.
A TipTap rich-text editor and dnd-kit drag-and-drop sorting speed up content and media management in the admin panel.
PWA support: a web app manifest and service worker enable caching and offline pages; production is hardened with Zod validation, Upstash rate-limiting and Playwright E2E tests.
caseStudy.outcome: Nexos Investment now manages listing and project data, the map, multilingual content and investor proposals from one system, fully under the consultants' own control. Hand-built presentations have given way to automatically generated PDF/PowerPoint proposals, and listings are updated across every language from a single panel. The firm moved past the limits of off-the-shelf themes into a scalable technical foundation built around its own workflow.

ambalaj-cini.title: Ambalaj Cini
ambalaj-cini.summary: E-commerce + ad management — 30% company growth via Google Ads and Meta campaigns.
body: For Bilecik-based Ambalaj Cini we led development of the Next.js/React online sales platform: payment integration, product management and the order flow in one system.

Alongside development we set up and managed Google Ads and Facebook (Meta) campaigns — these digital growth efforts drove 30% company growth. Concrete, results-driven proof of our ad management service.

caseStudy.challenge: Bilecik-based Ambalaj Cini needed a platform to sell packaging and cleaning products online while managing orders, stock, shipping and invoicing from one place. Its existing setup lacked the flexibility to handle a growing catalog and rising order volume; payment collection, shipment tracking and internal operations (stock, accounting, CRM) all ran separately. The company wanted a fast, secure shopping experience for customers on one side, and a back office to run the entire operation from a single panel on the other.
caseStudy.solution: We built an e-commerce system on Next.js and PostgreSQL (database, authentication, file storage) that combines the customer storefront with a full back office in one platform. The storefront covers catalog, promotions, cart and order/shipment tracking; the admin panel handles product/stock, orders, shipping, invoicing, accounting, CRM and campaign management with role-based access (admin/staff). Payment collection is automated through the PayTR iFrame API and shipping through a DHL integration, with order status and shipment status synced in both directions. On security, admin logins require multi-factor authentication (TOTP), Upstash-based rate limiting and a Content-Security-Policy are in place, and customers can manage their own data under Turkey's KVKK data-protection law. Pricing is always calculated server-side from the database; mutations run through Zod-validated Next.js Server Actions. Critical flows are covered by Vitest unit tests and Playwright E2E tests.
highlights: Card payment collection via the PayTR iFrame API and shipment tracking via a DHL integration stay synced in both directions with order status.
multi-factor authentication (TOTP) is mandatory in the admin panel; an account-owner rule plus Upstash rate-limiting block unauthorized access and brute-force attempts.
Price is always calculated server-side from the database; mutations run through Server Actions with Zod validation, so a client-submitted amount is never trusted.
Web push notifications (VAPID) and Resend transactional emails deliver order, payment and stock status changes to customers and the team instantly.
Vitest unit tests and Playwright E2E tests (covering auth, payment, shipping, search and other critical flows) validate every change on the CI pipeline.
caseStudy.outcome: Ambalaj Cini now runs catalog, order, payment, shipping and accounting workflows end to end from one system, with its own team. Card payments and shipment tracking are automated, admin access is secured with multi-factor authentication, and customer and team notifications go out instantly. Alongside development, the Google Ads and Meta campaigns we ran drove 30% growth for the company.

odeme-takip-botu.title: Payment Tracker Bot
odeme-takip-botu.summary: Payment-tracking web app that sends automatic Telegram reminders as due dates approach.
body: We built a web app that monitors company payments (installments, cheques, cash and more) and sends automatic Telegram reminders as due dates approach — on a lightweight, reliable Node.js, Express and SQLite stack.

Auto-generated installment schedules, dashboards for overdue and next-7-days payments, and financial-integrity safeguards for settled records make it a concrete example of automating business workflows.

caseStudy.challenge: The company was tracking credit-card installments, cheques, cash payments and other payment types by hand; forgotten due dates created late-payment risk, and payments were kept in different notebooks or spreadsheets by different people. What it needed was a lightweight but reliable system that could run on a single server without a separate ops team or complex infrastructure, while automating due-date tracking and alerting the right people on time. It also had to keep settled records from being altered by accident during edits, and export period-end reports with Turkish characters intact.
caseStudy.solution: We built a server-rendered web app with Node.js, Express and EJS, backed by a single-file SQLite database via better-sqlite3. For installment payments, a monthly schedule is generated automatically from the first due date, including correction for month-end overflow; amounts are balanced on the last installment so no fraction of a currency unit is lost. node-cron runs a due-date check every day at 09:00, a daily summary at 08:00, and a weekly plan message every Monday at 08:15, all delivered via the Telegram Bot API; a notification log table guarantees the same reminder is never sent twice for the same due date. Authentication hashes passwords with bcrypt and stores sessions in a file-based store (session-file-store), so sessions survive a server restart. The payments page offers a filter-aware CSV export with a UTF-8 BOM and semicolon separators. The interface is built with compiled Tailwind CSS, served with no CDN dependency.
highlights: Installment-schedule automation: monthly installments generate automatically from the first due date, month-end overflow is corrected, and any rounding difference is balanced onto the last installment.

Three separate automations run through the Telegram Bot API: a single due-date reminder (lead time configurable), a daily summary (08:00) and a weekly plan (Monday 08:15) — all scheduled with node-cron.
A notification log table (a uniqueness constraint on installment_id + window_days) stops the same reminder from ever being sent more than once.
Editing a payment that already has a settled installment never regenerates the due-date schedule — payment history stays intact.
A UTF-8 BOM, semicolon-separated CSV export respects active filters and displays Turkish characters correctly straight in Excel.
caseStudy.outcome: The company now tracks every payment type from a single panel and no longer has to remember due dates by hand; automatic Telegram reminders plus daily and weekly summaries have cut late-payment risk. Settled records stay protected during edits, so financial history remains trustworthy; period-end reporting is faster with a filter-aware CSV export, and sessions survive a server restart without interruption.

holly-trader.title: Holly Trader
holly-trader.summary: Trading and analysis tool prototype built on Node.js.
body: Holly Trader is a Node.js-based tool prototype that monitors market data and produces trading analyses. Data collection, signal generation and reporting flow through a single service.
This fintech product experiment is a side project demonstrating real-time data processing and automation capability.

caseStudy.challenge: Holly Trader is a fintech product experiment Piton Studios launched on its own — there is no real exchange client or live capital behind it. The goal was to build, inside a monorepo with clean backend/frontend/package boundaries, an end-to-end trading infrastructure that enforces leveraged-trading risk on the server side, brings multiple asset classes (crypto, equities, commodities) under one roof, and can run automated strategies against real-time market data. The real challenge was keeping market data streamed over WebSocket, order/position state and risk limits in a single, consistently synchronized state.
caseStudy.solution: The backend was built on NestJS with REST, WebSocket and BullMQ-based queues; Prisma and PostgreSQL handle the data layer, Redis handles queuing and caching. The Binance integration groups spot, futures, wallet and user-stream services into separate modules, with separate market-data services covering equities, commodities and DEX data. Authentication supports classic JWT login alongside ethers-based wallet (MetaMask) signature login. A RiskService validates leverage, exposure and margin ratio server-side before every order; a dedicated stop-loss/take-profit monitor and trailing-stop service check open positions periodically, and a reconciliation service compares exchange state against local data. The strategy engine runs ready-made strategies — grid bot, DCA, RSI mean-reversion, MACD crossover, breakout and scalping — through a shared interface, backed by a separate BullMQ-queued backtesting service. The frontend is built on Next.js 14; live data arriving via socket.io-client feeds into Zustand and React Query state, with lightweight-charts and recharts powering the analysis interface.
highlights: RiskService validates every order server-side against leverage, margin and exposure limits — the check is never left to the client.
The Binance integration groups spot, futures, wallet and WebSocket streaming into separate services, including funding and sync jobs.
BullMQ- and Redis-based queues process order execution, price alerts and analytics calculations in the background.

Eight ready-made strategies (grid bot, DCA, RSI mean-reversion, MACD crossover, breakout, scalping, multi-timeframe, custom) run through a shared strategy interface, backed by a dedicated backtesting engine.
Authentication works via JWT or an ethers-based wallet signature (MetaMask); a reconciliation service continuously compares exchange state against local data.
caseStudy.outcome: The result is a trading-infrastructure prototype that unifies crypto, equity and commodity markets in one interface while enforcing risk on the server side. Backend and frontend live in separate packages that share common types through a shared package. The project is a side venture demonstrating our technical capability in real-time data processing, queued job execution and multi-exchange integration — it makes no claim of live capital or trading performance.

velair-experience.title: VELAIR
velair-experience.summary: Scroll-driven cinematic 3D private-jet experience — cloud transition, opening cabin and fly-by.
body: VELAIR is a concept that turns the private-jet experience into a cinematic, scroll-driven 3D story. A top-down jet view, a shader-based cloud transition, an opening cabin and a side fly-by behind a panel all unfold in one natural scroll flow; the aircraft is an original parametric model generated in code.

Built with Next.js, React Three Fiber, Drei and GSAP ScrollTrigger, a single progress value drives the camera, the jet and the clouds, with no continuous rendering while idle. A reduced-motion option, static images rendered from the same model when WebGL is unavailable, and mobile-specific framing keep performance and accessibility in balance.

caseStudy.challenge: VELAIR is a concept Piton Studios launched on its own initiative — there is no real client or aircraft manufacturer behind it. The goal was to build a private-jet-themed portfolio piece on original geometry generated in the browser, rather than purchased 3D models or video footage; to blend a top-down view, a cloud transition, a cabin reveal and a horizontal flight into one seamless, natural scroll flow; and to keep the experience readable on devices without WebGL support, under a reduced-motion preference, and on narrow mobile screens — all while holding performance steady with a single canvas and a single playhead.
caseStudy.solution: In the Next.js App Router, content stays a server component while the Three.js scene lazy-loads only on the client. The aircraft is a parametric geometry built and assembled piece by piece in the browser — there is no downloaded 3D model file. A single GSAP ScrollTrigger produces one 0–1 progress value, which a pure function converts into camera, jet and cloud pose, while a separate helper adjusts zoom and mobile framing to viewport height. The scene renders on demand: frames are drawn only when the user scrolls, with no per-frame React state or DOM measurement. When WebGL2 isn't supported, on context loss, or under a reduced-motion preference, the experience falls back to static posters rendered from the same model; cabin-selection buttons are accessible to screen readers. Section boundaries, pose sampling and mobile framing are covered by automated tests run with the Node test runner.
highlights: The aircraft isn't an imported GLB — it's an original geometry built and assembled parametrically in the browser.
A single GSAP ScrollTrigger progress value drives the camera, the jet and the cloud shader together; no per-frame React state is used.
On-demand rendering: the scene redraws only on scroll, so no GPU work is spent while idle, with device pixel ratio capped to a 1–1.5 range.
A seamless fallback to static posters rendered from the same model when WebGL2 is unsupported, on context loss, or under a reduced-motion preference.
Automated tests for section boundaries, pose sampling and mobile framing run with the Node test runner.
caseStudy.outcome: The result is a live concept demo that carries visitors through six sections in one uninterrupted scroll flow. Staying readable without WebGL, under reduced motion, and on mobile, it stands as a reference showcasing our 3D storytelling and motion-design capability. As we note in our own documentation, a licensed artist model and device-level performance benchmarking are subjects for the next production round.

process.desc: Content source for the chatbot (docs, FAQ, product data) is prepared; message templates are designed for WhatsApp flows.

process.title: Integration
process.desc: Notification/sales flow via Twilio or Meta Cloud API, plus a RAG-based chatbot integration on your site.

process.title: Response Quality Testing
process.desc: Assistant responses are tested against representative questions; the human-handoff threshold and guardrails are tuned here.

process.title: Launch & Monitoring
process.desc: Go-live, response log monitoring, and content updates based on questions observed in the first weeks.

faq.q: Do we need Meta's approval to set up the WhatsApp Business API?
faq.a: Yes, WhatsApp Business API use is subject to Meta's own policies and approval process; account verification and template approvals are handled on the client's behalf, and timing can vary on Meta's side.

faq.q: Will the assistant you add to our site make things up?
faq.a: The assistant draws answers from your content rather than general model knowledge (RAG), which significantly lowers that risk — and it hands the conversation to a human instead of answering when it isn't confident.

faq.q: Is our data used to train the model?
faq.a: Under enterprise API plans, data sent is not used for model training by default; since this varies by provider, we verify the current terms with you on every project rather than assuming.

faq.q: Can you integrate the WhatsApp automation with our existing CRM?
faq.a: Yes — we can wire notification and sales flows to your CRM, order system, or another data source on a trigger basis.

meta-ads.title: Meta Ads
meta-ads.desc: Facebook and Instagram ad campaigns built around conversions, not vanity metrics.
meta-ads.longDesc: We run Meta ads (Facebook and Instagram) built around your actual conversion goal — not likes or reach. Campaign structure, audience segmentation, and creative production all tie back to a single conversion logic: no budget goes out before Meta Pixel and Conversions API are set up correctly. We're listed on the site as a Meta Partner.

features.title: Campaign Architecture
features.desc: Campaign structure that separates awareness, consideration, and conversion stages — with goals and budget matched to each.

features.title: Creative Production
features.desc: Static, video, and carousel ad creative designed for how people actually scroll through Meta's feed.

features.title: Audience & Retargeting
features.desc: Custom audiences, lookalikes, and retargeting segments so budget reaches the right people.

features.title: Pixel & Conversions API
features.desc: Meta Pixel and server-side Conversions API set up together — reliable conversion data that doesn't depend on browser trackers.

features.title: Creative Testing
features.desc: Systematic creative and messaging tests; underperforming ads are refreshed on a regular cycle.

features.title: Reporting
features.desc: Weekly reports focused on business metrics — leads, revenue, ROAS — not vanity metrics.

process.title: Audit & Setup
process.desc: Existing account audit (or new account setup), Meta Pixel and Conversions API implementation, and baseline measurement.

process.title: Campaign Build
process.desc: Campaign structure, audience segmentation, creative production, and ad copy.

process.title: Launch & Learn
process.desc: The learning phase is tracked with daily monitoring. No major changes until the algorithm has sufficient data.

process.title: Optimize
process.desc: Weekly optimization cycles: creative refreshes, audience narrowing/expansion, budget allocation.

process.title: Scale
process.desc: Proven campaigns scaled methodically. Budget increases tied to efficiency thresholds, not ambition.

faq.q: Do Meta ads work differently from Google Ads?
faq.a: Yes. Google Ads is built on intent-based search; Meta is built on audience targeting and creative. We manage them with different strategies, often together.

faq.q: How long until we see results?
faq.a: Meta's learning phase depends on the number of weekly optimization events per campaign; expect 1-2 weeks of learning before optimization starts paying off.

faq.q: Do you work with existing campaigns?
faq.a: Yes. We audit the account and Pixel/Conversions API setup first, identify the biggest losses, and fix those before building new campaigns.

faq.q: Is the management fee separate from ad spend?
faq.a: Yes. You pay Meta directly for ad spend. Our management fee is separate and covers strategy, creative production, and optimization.

maintenance-support.title: Maintenance & Support
maintenance-support.desc: Post-launch updates, security, and monitoring — monthly care that keeps the system as solid as it launched.
maintenance-support.longDesc: Launch isn't an ending for us. After delivery we offer an ongoing maintenance process that keeps the system running, dependencies current, and small change requests moving instead of piling up in a queue. Scope varies by project: some clients want only security patches and monitoring, others add regular small improvements every month.

features.title: Security Patches
features.desc: Dependencies and infrastructure are updated regularly; known vulnerabilities are assessed and patched as soon as they surface.

features.title: Backups
features.desc: Built on the daily automated backups and managed infrastructure of hosting providers like Vercel and Google Cloud; critical projects get a separately defined disaster-recovery procedure.

features.title: Uptime Monitoring
features.desc: The team is alerted the moment the system goes down or error rates spike — issues are caught before users report them.

features.title: Small Changes
features.desc: Text updates, minor UI tweaks, or content additions are handled under the maintenance plan without a separate quote for each request.

features.title: Dependency Updates
features.desc: Framework and library versions are updated on a regular cadence, so the system doesn't accumulate technical debt over time.

features.title: Monthly Report
features.desc: Updates made, issues found, and recommended next steps are shared in a short monthly report.

process.title: Scope Definition
process.desc: We clarify which services (security, monitoring, small changes) fall under the plan and the expected response cadence.

process.title: Monitoring Setup
process.desc: Error tracking, uptime checks, and backup verification are put in place before the maintenance plan starts.

process.title: Maintenance Schedule
process.desc: The update and patch cadence is set — critical security patches take priority, routine updates run on a planned interval.

process.title: Request Handling
process.desc: Small change requests are collected in a queue and worked through according to plan scope.

process.title: Monthly Review
process.desc: A short call reviews what was done and sets priorities for the following month together.

faq.q: Do you provide support after launch?
faq.a: Yes. Bug fixes are covered under warranty for a defined period after delivery; scope and length are written into the contract up front. Once the warranty period ends, ongoing support moves to a maintenance plan.

faq.q: What happens with backups and outages?
faq.a: We choose hosting platforms that offer daily automated backups and managed infrastructure; recovery largely relies on those providers' own infrastructure guarantees. For critical projects, a disaster-recovery procedure is defined separately during the architecture phase.

faq.q: Does the maintenance plan include adding small features?
faq.a: Minor UI tweaks and content changes can be considered within scope; a new module or substantial feature development is priced as a separate line item.

faq.q: What if we want to hand maintenance off to another team later?
faq.a: Since the code and documentation are yours, handover is possible; we provide a document explaining how the system works and, if needed, a short handover call.
