We've delivered the first on five projects; for the second, we'd adapt the auth, admin panel and real-time-feature infrastructure we built for Nexos Investment and Emlak Sync to the transfer sector. Which scale you should start at depends on your daily booking volume and fleet size; we settle that question together in the first conversation, so you're not investing in unnecessary complexity from the outset. For most companies the right starting point is to build the request form first and move to a platform as booking volume grows.
detail.2: For Jet Transfer Cyprus and Aydın Transfer we combined online booking with route and price calculation tools; for Kıbrıs Lefkoşa Taksi and Kardeşler Taxi we wired one-tap calling and a WhatsApp flow into a mobile-first design; for Welcome Pickups we built a multilingual structure and customer reviews into a booking experience that builds trust with international travelers. Local SEO work accompanied the booking flow on all five projects, because a form that captures requests only pays off once the customer can find the site in the first place. These five projects are a real, working solution that doesn't go beyond a request form but takes real pressure off the phone line -- and setup time was kept short to match.
detail.3: Once the fleet grows, or needs like online payment, vehicle assignment and a driver panel emerge, this structure turns into a web application. We don't yet have a project at that scale in the transfer sector, and we say so plainly. But the auth, admin panel and real-time-feature architecture we built for Nexos Investment can be applied to transfer booking with the same approach: role-based access, live status updates and reporting are all built on the same foundation. We decide together, based on your needs, which scale to start at -- starting with a small request form and expanding into a platform over time is also a valid option. Because we build the data model correctly from the start, your existing booking history carries over into the new system without loss whenever that transition happens.

hotel-booking-website.title: Hotel Website & Booking
hotel-booking-website.metaTitle: Hotel Website & Booking System | Piton Studios
hotel-booking-website.metaDescription: We design photo-gallery-driven hotel websites with a custom-coded booking flow and multilingual structure. Example: the Sammys Hotel boutique property site.
hotel-booking-website.intro: A hotel website is a showcase where the guest decides based on the photos and how easy booking is. For Sammys Hotel we built a booking system custom-coded to the hotel's own workflow instead of an off-the-shelf plugin: room selection, dates and requests all integrated into brand-specific design. We adapt the same approach to hospitality businesses of every size.

bullets.1: The photo gallery carries the site -- guests explore the room and the property before they ever arrive.
bullets.2: A booking system that integrates room selection, dates and requests into brand-specific design.
bullets.3: Multilingual presentation -- a guest reading a page in their own language trusts it more easily.
bullets.4: Mobile-first speed -- travel research happens mostly on phones.
bullets.5: SEO optimization increases the hotel's visibility in international searches.

hotel-booking-website.painTitle: Where hotel sites get stuck on the web

painPoints.1: Sales run entirely through booking platforms; every stay pays a commission.
painPoints.2: Photos are outdated or thin; guests can't be sure they'll get what they see when they arrive at the site.
painPoints.3: An off-the-shelf booking plugin doesn't match the hotel's actual room types, seasons and request flow, so the guest ends up having to call anyway.

hotel-booking-website.ctaText: Let guests see the room and book directly with you -- let's talk about your hotel website.

detail.1: A hotel website and booking solution has to carry two things at once: visual presentation that convinces the guest, and a booking flow that doesn't lose them. An off-the-shelf booking plugin often doesn't quite fit a hotel's actual room types, seasonal pricing or special requests, so designing the flow from scratch around the hotel's own workflow gives a more reliable result. In a photo-heavy site, performance is also critical, so the balance between gallery and speed has to be built in from the start -- a visitor won't wait for a slow-loading gallery on their phone before moving to another option. How many steps the booking flow takes is also determined by the hotel's actual operations -- number of room types, seasonal pricing, special requests.
detail.2: That's exactly what we did for Sammys Hotel: instead of an off-the-shelf plugin, we built a booking system custom-coded to the hotel's workflow -- room selection, dates and requests all integrated into brand-specific design. We made the photo gallery carry the site, and delivered a stylish digital showcase reaching international tourists through a multilingual structure and SEO optimization. This project is one of our strongest proofs of custom feature development capability; instead of squeezing the hotel's own operations into an off-the-shelf plugin's template, the system itself became the hotel's operation, and the guest experience benefited directly. The booking form and photo gallery were built in the same design language, as a single flow.
detail.3: The outcome is that guests book directly with you rather than through a platform -- no commission in between, and the guest relationship starts with you from the very first request. Today, Sammys Hotel is our only example in this exact mold in our portfolio, and we say so plainly. But we apply the same approach -- booking logic custom to real operations, gallery-driven design, multilingual structure and SEO -- to hotels, boutique stays and guesthouses of every size; we build the flow around your own room and season setup, rather than squeezing you into an off-the-shelf template. We start the first conversation by mapping your hotel's booking flow together; your room types, season calendar and guest profile become the starting point for the design, not a template.

ecommerce-automation.title: E-commerce Automation
ecommerce-automation.metaDescription: We build n8n and webhook-based automation workflows that sync stock, orders and marketplace listings for e-commerce stores; scope is defined together with you.
ecommerce-automation.intro: E-commerce automation connects the order, payment, shipping and notification steps in your store instead of running them by hand. For Ambalaj Cini we built infrastructure that keeps payment collection, DHL shipment tracking and order status in sync and sends automatic notifications to customers and staff; we apply the same approach to stock and marketplace synchronisation.

bullets.1: Webhook flows that automatically update stock, shipping and accounting systems when an order comes in.
bullets.2: Multi-marketplace listing and stock sync with n8n or Zapier.
bullets.3: Automatic order and return notifications sent by email or WhatsApp.
bullets.4: Scheduled jobs that automate stock reports, invoicing and recurring maintenance tasks.
bullets.5: Failure-alert monitoring -- the team is notified instantly the moment a sync step breaks.

ecommerce-automation.painTitle: The problems a lack of automation creates in e-commerce

painPoints.1: When stock is updated by hand across multiple systems, orders keep coming in even after a product has sold out.
painPoints.2: When order, invoice and shipping information sit in separate tables, there's no way to track which order is at which stage.
painPoints.3: Without marketplace integration, a store has to enter listings and update stock by hand on every platform.

ecommerce-automation.ctaText: Let's put your repetitive manual work into automation -- let's talk about your e-commerce automation needs.

detail.1: E-commerce automation doesn't target the store itself (catalog, payment, order flow) -- it targets connecting those systems to the outside world: marketplaces, shipping, accounting, customer communication. In our automation service we start by mapping the process: who does the manual work, at which step, with which decision. Then we decide which tool fits the job -- n8n (on your own infrastructure, no per-execution fee, no vendor lock-in) or Zapier (fast setup with no infrastructure overhead); we usually move complex flows to n8n. The goal is to eliminate repetitive work that shouldn't require a person; error handling and edge cases are documented and designed before implementation, not patched on afterward. An automation built this way stays easy to update whenever a business rule changes.
detail.2: The clearest example of this approach is Ambalaj Cini: payment collection via PayTR and shipment tracking via the DHL integration stay in two-way sync with order status, and order, payment and stock changes are sent automatically to both customers and the management team through web push notifications and transactional emails. On the marketplace side we adapt the logic of our own product, Emlak Sync: a record is entered once, published automatically to several portals (101evler, HangiEv) and kept in sync, eliminating duplicate data entry. The same principle — enter once, distribute automatically to several systems — applies to stock and marketplace synchronisation. We adapt this experience to your store's own systems (stock, shipping, accounting), starting with the manual step that costs the most time and expanding scope step by step.
detail.3: After setup, we keep the process observable with failure alerts, execution logs and dashboards; if a sync step breaks, you see it before orders pile up. Scope depends on the store's size and the number of systems it connects to; in the first conversation we work out together which manual task is the best fit for automation. At handover we document the process and train your team to maintain it, and we offer support for ongoing changes -- updating the automation together as the system evolves. That way automation isn't a one-time project but infrastructure that grows with your store, connecting to any new system with the same logic when it's added; we settle scope, complexity and timeline together based on your store's actual needs.

restaurant-google-ads.title: Google Ads for Restaurants
restaurant-google-ads.metaTitle: Google Ads Management for Restaurants | Piton Studios
restaurant-google-ads.metaDescription: Google Ads management that brings new customers to restaurants and cafes through search campaigns, with setup and tracking tied to your reservation page.
restaurant-google-ads.intro: We build and manage Google Ads campaigns that put your restaurant in front of searches like 'restaurant near me' at the right moment. A campaign shouldn't just earn clicks -- it should turn them into filled tables by connecting to your menu page and reservation flow, ahead of local SEO taking hold.

bullets.1: Local-search-focused campaign structure -- we target high-intent searches like 'area + restaurant/cafe' instead of spending budget on broad, irrelevant impressions.
bullets.2: Ad copy aligned with your menu and reservation page -- what the ad promises matches what visitors see on the site, so no click goes to waste.
bullets.3: Time-of-day optimization -- budget increases around lunch and dinner hours and pulls back when you're closed.
bullets.4: Conversion tracking -- concrete actions like reservation requests and directions clicks are measured, so you see which campaign actually brings customers to the table.
bullets.5: Weekly reporting -- spend, clicks and incoming requests are shared in a plain report, no agency jargon needed to make a decision.

restaurant-google-ads.painTitle: Common mistakes restaurants make with Google Ads

painPoints.1: A campaign set up with broad match gets impressions from outside the area or from irrelevant searches; budget runs out fast but tables stay empty.
painPoints.2: The ad gets clicked, but the landing page shows an outdated menu or loads slowly; the visitor leaves before ever reaching the reservation step.
painPoints.3: With no conversion tracking in place, no one knows which campaign is actually bringing in customers, so budget gets allocated by guesswork.

restaurant-google-ads.ctaText: Let's talk about a Google Ads campaign for your restaurant -- write to us.

detail.1: For restaurants and cafes, the job of Google Ads is to move the person searching in the right area at the right time straight into your menu and reservation flow. Search intent in this sector is very clear -- the person is looking for somewhere to eat right now and decides within minutes; we build the campaign around that moment: keywords segmented by area and mealtime, a negative-keyword list that blocks irrelevant impressions, and ad copy that links straight to the menu page. Instead of spending budget on a generic 'restaurant' search, we focus on searches that already carry ordering or reservation intent -- and that difference means far more filled tables for the same budget.
detail.2: Before launching a campaign, we check whether the site itself is ready to receive it; the fast ordering flow we built for Boon Fresh and the clear menu presentation we designed for Virginia Ice Cream are examples of how a click turns into a decision. If your restaurant site is already with us, we connect the campaign directly to your existing menu and reservation page; if not, we get those pages ready first, because even a perfectly targeted ad falls flat when it hits a slow or outdated menu. Ad copy is written to mirror exactly what the site promises, so the person who clicks finds what they were looking for immediately and moves into the reservation or order step without friction. In the first two weeks after launch we hold off on major changes and let the data build, giving the algorithm room to learn.
detail.3: The outcome is a measured process, not a guess: the weekly report shows which keyword drives reservation requests and which hours convert best, and budget gradually shifts toward the campaigns that fill the most tables. As SEO and GEO work matures, organic visibility for searches like 'restaurant near me' grows too, and Google Ads' share can be reduced step by step -- but for as long as the campaign runs, the data it produces becomes lasting knowledge about which message and which time slot actually works. The report centers on incoming reservations and calls, not spend, so you can see whether the campaign is working by the numbers, not by impression.

finance-automation.title: Finance Process Automation
finance-automation.metaTitle: Finance Process Automation Services | Piton Studios
finance-automation.metaDescription: We build software for currency exchanges, crypto businesses and finance companies that automates payment tracking, reminders and reporting workflows.
finance-automation.intro: We build software for your finance company, currency exchange or crypto business that automates recurring processes like payment tracking, due-date reminders and reporting. With our own product, Payment Tracker Bot, we track due dates and send automatic reminders; Holly Trader collects and reports market data.

bullets.1: Due-date and reminder automation -- as a payment or installment date approaches, the right person gets an automatic notification via Telegram, email or WhatsApp.
bullets.2: Data collection and reporting -- market, rate or transaction data is gathered on a schedule and turned into a readable summary dashboard.
bullets.3: Custom internal tools -- a simple, reliable web panel your team can use daily replaces spreadsheets.
bullets.4: Financial-integrity safeguards -- settled records and historical data can't be accidentally altered during automation; every step stays auditable.
bullets.5: Phased rollout -- automation starts with the single process costing you the most time, then expands in scope once results are visible.

finance-automation.painTitle: The problems we see most often in finance processes

painPoints.1: Payment and due-date tracking is done by hand in spreadsheets; one skipped row means a late payment or a missed reminder.
painPoints.2: Market or rate data is compiled manually from different sources; putting a report together takes hours, and by the time it's ready the data is already stale.
painPoints.3: The whole process depends on one person's memory and attention; when that person is out or leaves, the system breaks down completely.

finance-automation.ctaText: Let's automate your finance process -- write to us.

detail.1: In finance, the value of automation shows up as much in eliminating errors as in speed; a miscalculated due date or a forgotten reminder means a direct financial loss. A well-built automation takes over the recurring work a person would otherwise do, freeing that person's attention for exceptions instead. As a manually maintained spreadsheet grows, so does the risk of error; automation keeps that risk flat by processing every row under the same rule. On time-sensitive work like due dates and amounts especially, that consistency doesn't slip even when the team is tired or on leave -- the system doesn't take holidays, doesn't forget, doesn't lose focus, and repeats every transaction with the same precision.
detail.2: We built this expertise into our own products: Payment Tracker Bot tracks company payments (credit card/installment, check, cash and other) and sends automatic reminders via Telegram as due dates approach; it generates due dates automatically for installment payments, gives a summary dashboard for overdue items and the next 7 days, and protects settled records from accidental changes. Holly Trader is a Node.js-based tool that collects, processes and reports market data -- data collection, signal generation and reporting all live in a single service. We adapt whichever model fits your finance company's process -- reminder-focused or data/reporting-focused -- to your project, and can combine both into one system if needed.
detail.3: When building automation, we never treat data security as separate from the process itself; where financial and personal data is stored and who can see it is settled at the design stage, and the system is built around that answer from the start. Rollout is phased, not all at once: we automate the single process costing the most time first, and expand scope as results become visible -- so your team sees the new system working at a small scale before trusting it fully. In the end, your team spends its time not updating a spreadsheet but reviewing the summary the automation produces and making decisions -- focused on growing the business rather than hunting for errors -- and workload doesn't scale up in lockstep with growth; the process scales before the team has to, and the system keeps working with the same discipline even as transaction volume rises.

corporate-ai-assistant.title: Corporate AI Assistant Development
corporate-ai-assistant.metaTitle: Corporate AI Assistant Development | Piton Studios
corporate-ai-assistant.metaDescription: We build AI assistants integrated into your corporate website or internal processes. Claude, OpenAI and Gemini, with guardrails and cost control built in.
corporate-ai-assistant.intro: We build AI assistants for your corporate website or internal processes that answer customer questions, search documents, or take over a repetitive task. We work with Claude, OpenAI and Gemini, choosing the model by use case rather than habit. Our own product experiment, ContentFlow AI, tested this integration experience firsthand.

bullets.1: Use-case definition -- what the assistant will answer, what data it can access, and what it should never do are defined upfront.
bullets.2: RAG and document-based responses -- the assistant answers from your own organization's documents and content, not mixed with general internet knowledge.
bullets.3: Guardrails and scope limits -- the assistant doesn't stray outside its defined topic; filters reduce the risk of incorrect or misleading answers.
bullets.4: Cost control -- model selection and request management are designed so cost stays predictable as usage grows.
bullets.5: Traceability -- what data each answer was generated from, and its cost, is logged; the assistant never operates as a black box.

corporate-ai-assistant.painTitle: Common problems we see in corporate AI assistant projects

painPoints.1: The assistant launches as a generic model's default configuration; without scope defined around the organization's own process and content, answers end up off the mark.
painPoints.2: An assistant launched without guardrails tries to answer off-topic questions and can produce statements that create liability for the organization.
painPoints.3: Cost and usage weren't modeled upfront, so the bill becomes unpredictable as usage grows and the project loses its sustainability.

corporate-ai-assistant.ctaText: Let's talk about the right AI assistant for your organization -- write to us.

detail.1: A corporate AI assistant's value doesn't come from answering every query -- it comes from giving the right answer from the right source to the right query. That's why we start from the use case, not the model: will the assistant answer customer questions, search internal team documents, or fill out a repetitive form -- each scenario calls for a different architecture, different data access and a different guardrail set. Without that clarity, an assistant either stays too narrow to be useful or keeps an undefined scope and loses reliability -- both carry reputational risk for the organization and are hard to walk back.
detail.2: You've seen how we build multilingual structure and corporate trust on projects like BT Elevator and Arslan Group; on the AI-integration side, we tested our experience with our own product, ContentFlow AI -- a prototype that speeds up the steps from content idea to draft to publishing with AI, demonstrating our capability in model selection, flow design and productization. On corporate assistant projects we combine both experiences: we build an AI layer on top of the organization's existing content and process infrastructure, with a security and guardrail layer added in; we choose between Claude, OpenAI and Gemini by use case rather than habit, so we're never locked into a single provider.
detail.3: In the end, the goal is for the assistant to stay measurable and predictable. We track which questions get answered, where the assistant steps back, and how cost trends; what data each answer was generated from is logged. Internal data privacy and which data goes to which model is a design decision settled at the start of the integration -- not a safeguard bolted on afterward -- and it's reviewed throughout the process. That lets the organization manage the assistant as a system with defined responsibility rather than an experiment, able to explain in hindsight what was said and why -- making legal and reputational risk visible upfront.

education-platform.title: Education Platform Development
education-platform.metaTitle: Education Platform Development Services | Piton Studios
education-platform.metaDescription: We build custom education platforms with course, exam or student-tracking features. Enrollment flow, user panels and content management in one system.
education-platform.intro: When your course center or educational institution needs to go beyond a standard promotional site to features like student logins, progress tracking or exams, we build a custom web application. We don't yet have an education-sector project, but our listing-management portal for Nexos Investment and Social Pro's multi-account architecture prove the experience transfers.

bullets.1: Login-based structure -- a login and panel system runs with separate permissions for students, instructors and administrators.
bullets.2: Content and program management -- course and program content is updated from the panel with no technical knowledge required.
bullets.3: Progress and enrollment tracking -- which course a student is in, and at what stage, is visible from a single panel.
bullets.4: Scalable architecture -- a foundation that can grow from a small user base into a large platform without a rewrite.
bullets.5: Mobile-friendly interface -- students and parents get the same smooth experience when they access the platform from a phone.

education-platform.painTitle: The pattern we see most often when institutions need an education platform

painPoints.1: The institution starts with an off-the-shelf LMS but ends up patching the parts that don't fit its own process by hand, in spreadsheets.
painPoints.2: Without separate permission levels for students and instructors, everyone sees the same panel, and who should see what gets solved manually every time.
painPoints.3: Updating course content stays dependent on a developer; even a small change can take days.

education-platform.ctaText: Let's talk about your education platform needs -- write to us.

detail.1: Unlike a standard website, an education platform is a web application that requires user logins, permission levels and a proper data model. We start by answering whether the institution's need fits the mold of an off-the-shelf LMS or calls for a custom system built around its own process -- because every point where a ready-made system can't flex risks turning into a manually maintained spreadsheet later. The right answer depends on the institution's size, the variety of its programs and its team's technical capacity; that's why the first step is always a scoping conversation, not a pre-packaged solution -- we understand the institution's existing processes first, and the technology choice comes after.
detail.2: We haven't delivered an education-sector project yet, and we'd rather say so plainly than hide it -- and show the transferable experience we do have instead. For Nexos Investment we built a mapped, multilingual, permission-based portal spanning listing management all the way to automated PDF and presentation-format proposal generation; for our own product, Social Pro, we developed a multi-account architecture, content calendar and panel design from scratch. The student/instructor/administrator separation, content management and progress tracking an education platform needs rest on the same core principles as the architectures we built in these two projects: a correct data model, clear permissions, and content manageable from a panel. We choose the technology to match these principles and the scale of the project.
detail.3: The platform we deliver to an institution is built on a foundation that can grow without staying dependent on a developer -- a structure your content team can update itself, an architecture that doesn't need a rewrite as users grow. Throughout the process we scope things together and ship the first version in the narrowest form that still works, then build on top of it -- so the institution starts seeing results in its first enrollment period without waiting for the entire platform to be finished, and we shape the next step together based on feedback. This phased approach also keeps budget and scope from spiraling out of control -- you see clearly what you're paying for at each stage, and decide the next step based on real user feedback rather than a guess.

beauty-appointment-system.title: Beauty Salon Booking System
beauty-appointment-system.metaTitle: Beauty Salon Booking System Development | Piton Studios
beauty-appointment-system.metaDescription: Custom booking systems for salons and hairdressers with staff- and service-based scheduling. Clients book online, the salon manages it all from one panel.
beauty-appointment-system.intro: For salons and hairdressers that want a custom booking system beyond a standard appointment form -- one that shows availability by staff member and service duration -- we build a web application. We don't yet have a beauty-sector project in our portfolio, but our booking-flow work for Jet Transfer Cyprus and Welcome Pickups adapts directly to a salon's calendar.

bullets.1: Staff- and service-based calendar -- the client picks a service and, if they want, a staff member, and the system shows only genuinely available slots.
bullets.2: Automatic reminders -- clients get an automatic SMS or WhatsApp reminder before their appointment, cutting the no-show rate.
bullets.3: Salon panel -- the owner sees every appointment, staff availability and cancellation from one panel.
bullets.4: Online payment or deposit integration -- when requested, taking a deposit at booking reduces the risk of an empty slot.
bullets.5: Mobile-first flow -- a client completes a booking from their phone in a few taps, with no back-and-forth messaging.

beauty-appointment-system.painTitle: The pattern we see most often when salons move to a booking system

painPoints.1: Appointments come in through DMs and phone calls; which staff member is free at which hour lives only in the receptionist's memory.
painPoints.2: No reminder goes out for a no-show client, and that empty appointment slot can never be recovered.
painPoints.3: Off-the-shelf booking software doesn't quite fit the salon's own service and staff structure, so the business still ends up tracking part of it by hand.

beauty-appointment-system.ctaText: Let's talk about a custom booking system for your salon -- write to us.

detail.1: In a beauty salon, a booking system isn't a simple form -- it's a small operations tool that manages staff availability, service duration and client preference all at once. The need usually is a shift from manual tracking that depends on one person to a system where multiple staff calendars run without conflict; as a salon grows, that shift stops being a luxury and becomes necessary to maintain service quality. A poorly planned booking system means both dissatisfied clients and wasted chair time -- both losses hit revenue directly and compound over time; even a small hiccup can turn into reputational damage, because a client is only ever a message away from another salon.
detail.2: We haven't delivered a beauty-sector project yet, and we'd rather show its transferable side than hide that fact. At Jet Transfer Cyprus we built an online booking flow combined with route and price calculation tools; at Welcome Pickups we built a multilingual, review-backed, mobile-first booking system. The core problem we solved on those projects -- showing accurate availability, capturing requests in a structured format and presenting them to the business on a clear panel -- rests on the exact same logic as staff- and service-based scheduling for a salon; only the 'route' becomes 'service and staff', while the backbone of the flow stays the same.
detail.3: The system we build takes shape around the salon's day-to-day operation: how many staff there are, how long each service takes, whether a deposit will be taken, and which channel reminders go out on. The first version ships answering those questions in the narrowest scope, and layers like reminders, payment or reporting get added on as the salon uses it -- so the salon never pays upfront for a feature it doesn't need, and grows the system at its own pace. This approach lets both a small salon and a large chain get a system sized to their own scale; neither pays extra for the other's needs, and the system matures based on real usage rather than carrying unnecessary complexity from day one.

whatsapp-sales-bot.title: WhatsApp Sales & Order Bot
whatsapp-sales-bot.metaDescription: We build a WhatsApp bot for your online store that sends order-status updates, abandoned-cart reminders and answers product questions, Meta-approved.
whatsapp-sales-bot.intro: Your customers now open WhatsApp to ask where their order is, get reminded about an abandoned cart, or ask a quick product question. A bot that answers order status, cart reminders and product questions automatically handles that faster than email ever could.

bullets.1: Order-status notifications -- shipped, out for delivery, delivered: each trigger sends an automatic WhatsApp message to the customer.
bullets.2: Abandoned-cart reminders -- if checkout isn't completed within a set window, a gentle reminder goes out automatically.
bullets.3: Product Q&A -- stock, size, delivery time and other common questions are answered from your own store data (RAG), not general internet knowledge.
bullets.4: Human handoff -- when the bot isn't confident or the customer insists, the conversation is routed to your team automatically.
bullets.5: Integration with your existing store -- notifications hook into your real order and inventory data, not a manually triggered list.

whatsapp-sales-bot.painTitle: Where WhatsApp gets wasted in e-commerce

painPoints.1: Order-status questions get answered one by one, by hand, on WhatsApp; on a busy day this alone becomes a full-time job.
painPoints.2: Abandoned carts never get a reminder -- a customer adds an item, leaves, and the sale disappears without a trace.
painPoints.3: Product questions go through email and take hours to answer -- by then the customer has already bought elsewhere.

whatsapp-sales-bot.ctaText: Let's build a WhatsApp sales bot for your store -- tell us about the project and we'll plan Meta's approval process together.

detail.1: WhatsApp has become more than a support channel in e-commerce -- it's now the primary place customers ask about order status, expect a nudge when they abandon a cart, and look for a fast answer about a product. All three needs run on the same infrastructure: trigger-based flows on the WhatsApp Business API, plus an assistant that answers from your own store data. Meta's verification and approval process is part of the project from day one -- account setup and template approvals are planned around it, not treated as a surprise blocker.
detail.2: We built and shipped WhatsApp notification automation for Gel Gez Gör: the system detects trending listings and sends an automatic WhatsApp message to the relevant person -- a trigger-based flow with no manual step. For Ambalaj Cini we built the e-commerce platform from scratch, including a back-office layer where order and stock data automatically becomes an internal notification. For your store, we apply the same trigger logic to order-status and cart-reminder flows -- this time aimed directly at the customer over WhatsApp. That experience taught us the operational side of trigger-based messaging as much as the technical one -- deciding exactly which event fires which message, and how retries are handled when a message fails to send.
detail.3: The product-Q&A layer is a separate piece: the assistant isn't a generic chatbot, it's a RAG system grounded in your product data, stock levels and delivery rules. The moment it isn't confident, or a customer pushes back, the conversation is automatically handed to your team instead of guessing an answer. During setup we define together which messages go out and which data feeds the assistant; after launch, content gets updated based on the real questions customers ask in the first weeks. That means the customer feels like they're talking to your brand, not a generic AI chatbot -- every answer traces back to your own catalog and policies, never to information pulled from outside them.

clinic-whatsapp-appointments.title: WhatsApp Appointment Bot for Clinics
clinic-whatsapp-appointments.metaDescription: We build a WhatsApp bot for clinics that takes appointment requests and sends reminders automatically, with patient data handled under clear privacy rules.
clinic-whatsapp-appointments.intro: Patients increasingly message a clinic on WhatsApp instead of calling to book or change an appointment. A bot that takes appointment requests and sends automatic reminders as the date approaches cuts phone traffic at the front desk while giving patients a faster response.

bullets.1: Appointment-request intake -- patients share their preferred day/time over WhatsApp, and the request reaches your team in a consistent format.
bullets.2: Automatic reminders -- as the appointment date approaches, the patient gets an automatic WhatsApp reminder, cutting no-shows caused by forgetting.
bullets.3: Common questions -- hours, address, which treatments are offered -- answered automatically from your clinic's own information.
bullets.4: Human handoff -- confirmation, treatment details or anything sensitive is routed to front-desk staff automatically, not answered by the bot.
bullets.5: Data-security first -- what patient data is stored where is settled at project start, not bolted onto the design afterward.

clinic-whatsapp-appointments.painTitle: Where the appointment process breaks down in clinics

painPoints.1: Appointment requests come in by phone; when the line is busy, the patient either waits or calls a different clinic.
painPoints.2: Without a reminder, patients forget -- and an empty slot that day can't be recovered.
painPoints.3: Even simple questions like hours and address eat into front-desk time that should go to the patients actually in front of them.

clinic-whatsapp-appointments.ctaText: Let's talk about a WhatsApp appointment bot for your clinic -- tell us your needs and we'll plan patient-data handling together.

detail.1: This isn't a medical assistant giving advice or diagnosis -- it's a WhatsApp automation for taking appointment requests, sending reminders and answering general information questions. The boundary is explicit: the assistant makes no treatment recommendation, and hands the conversation to front-desk staff the moment something sensitive or unclear comes up. Where patient data lives, who can access it, and how long it's retained is settled together at project start -- that decision is part of the design, not a patch added later. That clarity is what earns trust from both the clinic and the patient, and it's built into the technical architecture from the start, not patched on afterward.
detail.2: We built the corporate website for Dental Health, a clinic based in West New York -- service pages, a free-consultation call-out, and a design built around patient trust. That project gave us a close look at what a health-sector audience needs: reassuring communication, clear information, easy reachability; a WhatsApp appointment bot is the automation layer that takes that a step further. The trigger-based WhatsApp Business API flow itself is something we've shipped live -- on Gel Gez Gör -- and we adapt that same underlying logic to appointment requests and reminders.
detail.3: Setup integrates with your existing appointment system or shared calendar where one exists; reminder messages fire automatically off the appointment date, never sent by hand. WhatsApp Business API use is subject to Meta's approval process -- account verification and message-template approval are built into the project timeline from the start. After launch we track which questions reach the bot and which get handed to the front desk -- that feedback sharpens the line between what the bot answers and what staff should handle, over time. That means the system doesn't need rebuilding as the clinic grows or adds services -- only the content and rules get updated, which keeps the total cost of ownership down over time.

real-estate-meta-ads.title: Meta Ads for Real Estate Agencies
real-estate-meta-ads.metaTitle: Meta Ads for Real Estate | Piton Studios
real-estate-meta-ads.metaDescription: We run listing and lead-generation Meta ad campaigns for real estate agencies, targeting local and foreign buyers separately with Pixel and Conversions API.
real-estate-meta-ads.intro: A listing that reaches the right person on Facebook and Instagram converts to leads far better than site traffic alone ever does. We run listing and lead-focused Meta campaigns for real estate agencies -- built on Pixel and Conversions API, targeting local buyers and overseas buyers separately.

bullets.1: Listing/lead campaign structure -- each campaign is split into awareness, interest and lead-collection stages, with budget matched to each stage's goal.
bullets.2: Local vs. foreign buyer split -- a buyer searching locally in North Cyprus and an overseas investor get different ad copy and language, not the same message.
bullets.3: Meta Pixel + Conversions API -- every lead-form submission is measured accurately server-side, independent of browser trackers.
bullets.4: Creative production -- your property photo/video content becomes static, video and carousel ad creative built for how people scroll Meta's feed.
bullets.5: Weekly reporting -- lead count, cost per lead and which listing drove which campaign, tracked instead of likes or reach.

real-estate-meta-ads.painTitle: Where real estate agencies lose money on Meta ads

painPoints.1: One campaign shows the same language and message to both local and foreign buyers -- neither feels the ad was made for them.
painPoints.2: Pixel is set up but Conversions API isn't; browser trackers block a chunk of leads from ever being measured, and budget flows into a blind spot.
painPoints.3: Ads get judged on likes and reach; how many leads actually came in, and how many turned into a sale, is never tracked.

real-estate-meta-ads.ctaText: Let's set up a Meta ad campaign for your agency -- we can start with an audit of your existing account.

detail.1: The biggest failure point for Meta ads in real estate is audience separation: a local buyer house-hunting in North Cyprus and an overseas investor evaluating the same listing show up with completely different questions. We structure the campaign around that split -- awareness, interest and lead-collection are targeted separately, each with its own budget and creative. No budget goes out before Meta Pixel and server-side Conversions API are both in place, so lead data stays accurate regardless of browser trackers. That distinction goes beyond translation -- motivation, budget expectations and decision timelines differ between the two groups, and the campaign message is built to reflect that difference.
detail.2: We've run this exact discipline in live Meta ad management for Ambalaj Cini, combining Google Ads and Meta to contribute to 30% business growth -- Pixel and Conversions API setup was the infrastructure behind that result. Our real estate-specific experience sits on the project side: we built multilingual real estate sites for Nexos Investment and Pinnacle Yatırım, designed with the local/foreign buyer split in mind from the start. We bring both together into one campaign structure built for your listings. Bringing the two together gives you an ad-management approach that recognizes real estate's specific buyer behavior while still producing measurable results, not just impressions.
detail.3: Creative production starts from what you already have -- professional photography isn't a prerequisite; we turn your existing photo and video content into static, video and carousel formats built for how people scroll Meta's feed. Once a campaign launches, the learning phase is tracked daily, with no major changes until the algorithm has enough data. Weekly reporting runs on lead count and cost per lead, not likes or reach -- and because we track which listing drove which campaign, budget can shift toward the properties actually generating demand. That discipline means budget consistently flows toward listings that actually convert, not the ones that simply collect likes.

engineering-quote-portal.title: Technical Quote Portal for Engineering Firms
engineering-quote-portal.metaDescription: We build custom software for engineering firms that manages technical quotes and project requests in one panel, generating quote documents from your data.
engineering-quote-portal.intro: In engineering firms, quoting usually runs across scattered spreadsheets, email threads and hand-built files. A custom system that manages technical quotes and project requests in one panel -- generating documents automatically from the quote data -- keeps an engineer's time on the actual calculation, not file formatting.

bullets.1: Project-request intake -- every incoming request lands as one record with its technical details and client info, instead of getting lost in an email chain.
bullets.2: Auto-generated documents from quote data -- once line items, unit prices and technical notes are entered, the quote document (PDF) is generated automatically.
bullets.3: Status tracking -- every request shows a clear status -- draft, in progress, sent, approved -- so it's obvious whose desk it's sitting on.
bullets.4: Role-based access -- engineers, sales and management work in the same panel with different permissions, defined up front rather than patched in later.
bullets.5: Scalable data model -- adding a new project type or quote template doesn't require rewriting the system.

engineering-quote-portal.painTitle: Where the quoting process breaks down in engineering firms

painPoints.1: Every quote is built from scratch in a spreadsheet; the same calculation logic gets re-implemented slightly differently in different files, raising error risk.
painPoints.2: Project requests pile up in an inbox; there's no way to see whose request is at what stage.
painPoints.3: Building the quote document eats a meaningful share of an engineer's time -- hours that should go to actual technical work go into file formatting instead.

engineering-quote-portal.ctaText: Let's talk about a quote and project-request portal for your engineering firm -- describe your current process and we'll design it together.

detail.1: A technical quote portal is a different layer from a standard corporate website -- it's a workflow system that carries the process from request intake to finished quote document. We map the existing process first -- what information is collected when, what line items make up a quote, who signs off -- and build the system on top of that flow rather than forcing the process into an off-the-shelf template. Role-based access and a scalable data model are designed up front, so a new quote template doesn't break the system's foundation.
detail.2: We applied this exact approach at Nexos Investment: the system generates PDF and PowerPoint proposals automatically from listing data, eliminating the hand-built presentations a consultant used to prepare. On the Payment Tracker Bot project we built a custom system that consolidates internal records into one panel, with status tracking and role-based access. We also know the engineering sector closely from the Alert Mühendislik and BT Elevator projects -- a quote portal combines both strengths, built specifically for the sector's technical quoting workflow. Bringing these together produces a concrete system that lets an engineering firm run its entire quoting process end to end, from one panel.
detail.3: During setup we first bring your existing quote template and calculation logic into the system; the PDF output is designed to match your company's identity exactly. The PostgreSQL-based data model keeps quote history and client information in one place, so what was previously quoted to a given client becomes searchable. After delivery, the full source code is yours -- you're not locked into us to grow the system or add a new module. That keeps the entire quoting process inside one system -- reused line items stay consistent, pricing doesn't drift between quotes, and a new hire can be handed the right template immediately.

finance-customer-portal.title: Secure Customer Portal for Finance Companies
finance-customer-portal.metaDescription: We build a secure customer portal for finance companies that manages statements, documents and requests in one panel, with role-based access and an audit trail.
finance-customer-portal.intro: If showing a client their statement, a document, or a request's status still runs through email or a phone call, both sides are losing time. A customer portal that manages statements, documents and requests from one secure panel moves that information into a system the client can check themselves, and your team can manage from the same place.

bullets.1: Statement and document access -- clients log into their own account to view current statements and documents themselves, without asking your team.
bullets.2: Request management -- clients submit requests through the panel, with status (received, in progress, completed) clearly visible.
bullets.3: Role-based access -- clients see only their own data; your team accesses different records depending on their assigned role.
bullets.4: Audit trail -- who viewed or changed which record, and when, is traceable; settled records can't be accidentally altered.
bullets.5: Clarity on data location -- where data lives is decided together at project start, not a decision added on afterward.

finance-customer-portal.painTitle: Where client communication breaks down in finance companies

painPoints.1: Clients email or call to get their statement or a document; your team prepares and sends the same information by hand every time.
painPoints.2: The only way to check on a request's status is to call and ask; both sides end up repeating the same conversation.
painPoints.3: Records sit scattered across different systems and spreadsheets, with no clarity on where a given piece of data lives or who can access it.

finance-customer-portal.ctaText: Let's talk about a secure customer portal for your finance company -- describe your current process and we'll design data security together.

detail.1: When building a customer portal in finance, data security is the starting point of the design, not a feature added afterward. Where data lives, who can access which record, and how settled records stay protected are all settled together at project start; role-based access and an audit trail (who saw or changed what, and when) are built on top of that clarity. The portal works as one secure interface where a client can view their own statement and documents, submit a request, and track its status. That upfront agreement is what keeps the portal trustworthy as it scales, rather than becoming a liability later.
detail.2: Our experience building systems with financial integrity in mind is concrete on the Payment Tracker Bot project: we built a system where settled records can't be accidentally altered during automation, and overdue plus next-7-day payments surface on a summary dashboard. Halas Exchange gave us close exposure to the currency-exchange sector's client-communication needs, and Nexos Investment showed us how to build a scalable, role-based panel. We bring these three together to build your customer portal to the standard finance work demands. That combined experience means we build your customer portal as a system that understands finance's specific sensitivities, not just as a generic interface, and every decision reflects that.
detail.3: Setup starts by clarifying exactly what information clients see and which requests the panel collects. The PostgreSQL-based data model, role-based access and Zod validation target production-grade quality -- the same standard we apply across our other custom-software projects. After delivery, the source code is entirely yours; you're not locked into us to grow the system, and delivery includes documentation and team training. That standard is meant to serve not just today's needs but the new requests that surface as your business grows -- the data model is designed flexibly for that, so your team never has to rebuild the system as it scales, only extend it.

hotel-maintenance-care.title: Season-Proof Maintenance for Hotel Sites
hotel-maintenance-care.metaTitle: Hotel Site Maintenance Plan | Piton Studios
hotel-maintenance-care.metaDescription: We offer a maintenance plan for hotel and tourism sites built for seasonal traffic spikes: updates, backups and continuous booking-form monitoring.
hotel-maintenance-care.intro: The riskiest moment for a hotel site is when the booking form quietly breaks during the busiest week of the season -- days can pass before anyone notices. Our maintenance plan for hotel sites puts updates, backups and continuous booking-form monitoring under one responsibility, for the whole season, not just after launch.

bullets.1: Booking-form monitoring -- a submission error or outage triggers an immediate alert to the team, instead of quietly losing guests.
bullets.2: Pre-season checkup -- before the busy season starts, the site, form and integrations are tested one by one.
bullets.3: Automated backups -- built on the hosting provider's daily automated backups; critical projects can get a separately defined recovery procedure.
bullets.4: Security and dependency updates -- libraries and infrastructure are updated on a regular cadence, with known vulnerabilities patched as soon as they surface.
bullets.5: Small change requests -- a price update, room info or image change is handled under the plan, without a separate quote each time.

hotel-maintenance-care.painTitle: Where in-season maintenance falls through for hotel sites

painPoints.1: The booking form silently stops working because of an integration error; guests are lost for days before anyone notices.
painPoints.2: No pre-season check is done, so a problem surfaces during the busiest week -- exactly the worst possible time.
painPoints.3: Even a small text or price update needs a separate quote and waiting period every time, so requests just pile up.

hotel-maintenance-care.ctaText: Let's talk about a season-proof maintenance plan for your hotel site -- tell us about your current site and booking flow.

detail.1: In tourism, the week a website matters most is usually the week it gets watched the least -- the team is buried in operational load, and the site quietly runs unattended in the background. Our maintenance plan closes exactly that gap: the booking form and critical integrations are monitored continuously, so when an error or outage happens, the team knows before guests notice. Security patches and dependency updates run on a regular schedule -- critical ones get priority, routine ones follow a planned cadence. This approach guarantees the site gets watched most closely exactly when it needs it most -- during the very weeks bookings spike.
detail.2: We built Sammys Hotel's multilingual site with room booking and a photo gallery, which gave us a close look at how critical the booking flow and guest experience are on tourism sites. On Jet Transfer Cyprus we built a platform with a booking system and fare-calculation tools -- together, these two projects showed us exactly where booking-driven tourism sites tend to break. Our maintenance plan ties that observation to the monitoring and backup discipline of our general maintenance service. That observation is what makes our maintenance plan more than generic monitoring -- it's built with the specific attention tourism-sector sites need.
detail.3: Plan scope varies by project: some clients want only security patching and monitoring, others add regular small improvements every month. It's built on the hosting provider's (Vercel, Google Cloud) daily automated backups and managed infrastructure; critical projects get a separately defined disaster-recovery procedure at the architecture stage. A short monthly report shares what was updated, what issues were found, and what's recommended next -- not just after the season ends, but through it. That regular tracking prevents surprises from piling up by season's end -- planning for the next season starts much earlier, grounded in the previous season's reports, so the property builds on what came before instead of starting from zero every year.

real-estate-crm.title: CRM for Real Estate Agencies
real-estate-crm.metaTitle: CRM for Real Estate Agencies | Piton Studios
real-estate-crm.metaDescription: We build custom CRM systems tracking leads, portfolio matches, and viewing appointments for real estate agencies, drawing on our Nexos Investment experience.
real-estate-crm.intro: A real estate CRM is the internal system that shows which stage each lead is at, which listings they've been shown, and when the next viewing is. We haven't delivered a dedicated lead-and-viewing CRM for real estate yet; we adapt the panel architecture from Nexos Investment and the sync logic behind Emlak Sync.

bullets.1: Lead source, stage, and agent assignment on one screen — no inquiry sits forgotten in someone's inbox.
bullets.2: Listing-to-buyer matching — an agent sees every prospect interested in a given property in one list.
bullets.3: Viewing calendar with automatic reminders — a missed appointment doesn't have to mean a lost sale.
bullets.4: Role-based panel architecture — the same pattern we built for Nexos Investment, where owner, agent, and assistant work with different permissions.
bullets.5: Emlak Sync's single-source-of-truth logic keeps lead data from scattering across spreadsheets and WhatsApp threads.

real-estate-crm.painTitle: Where real estate agencies lose leads and listings

painPoints.1: When leads live across WhatsApp, calls, and spreadsheets, which stage a client is at exists only in an agent's memory.
painPoints.2: Without a shared viewing calendar, two agents can book the same property for the same time slot.
painPoints.3: When an agent leaves, the history of everyone they were following leaves the agency with them.

detail.1: A real estate CRM is a different layer from listing software: a listing site markets the property, a CRM manages the agent's relationship with the buyer — where the lead came from, which properties they've seen, what stage they're at, what the next step is. When that information lives in spreadsheets or an agent's personal notes, the number of leads that fall through the cracks grows with the agency; when an agent leaves, the entire relationship history goes with them. A properly built CRM instead unifies lead, listing, and appointment data in one model — the owner sees how many leads each agent is carrying at a glance, and client history survives staff turnover.
detail.2: Our experience here comes from two products: at Nexos Investment we built listing and project data management, multilingual content, and a role-based admin panel from scratch — a system architecture that runs an agency's daily work. At Emlak Sync we built the sync logic that lets a listing be entered once and published across multiple portals automatically; the same single-entry principle applies to lead and client data. We don't yet have a finished CRM project doing agent-level lead tracking and viewing scheduling — we say that plainly. But the panel architecture, role-based access, and sync experience from these two products are a direct foundation for building one.
detail.3: We start by mapping the agency's actual workflow: where leads come from, how many stages they pass through, who hands off to whom. We then turn that into a data model — lead record, listing match, viewing calendar, and reporting modules — and FurCRM's customer/account tracking and dealer management, though built for a different industry, carries the same architectural logic. Scope depends on agent count and lead volume; a small team might need only a simple lead list, while a growing agency prioritizes reporting and automated reminders sooner. As the system grows it can also connect to Emlak Sync's portal sync.

real-estate-crm.ctaText: Don't let leads disappear into spreadsheets — let's talk about your real estate CRM.

construction-erp.title: ERP for Construction Companies
construction-erp.metaTitle: ERP for Construction Companies | Piton Studios
construction-erp.metaDescription: We build custom ERP systems unifying project, subcontractor, progress-payment, and material tracking for construction firms, scoped to your company's workflow.
construction-erp.intro: A construction ERP shows which subcontractor is working on which project, what's owed based on completed progress, and how much material has gone to which site — all from one system. We don't have a construction-sector project at this scale yet; we adapt the production/dealer tracking from FurCRM and the stock/accounting back-office from Ambalaj Cini to a construction workflow.

bullets.1: Project-level view — each site is tracked as its own record, with its own budget, progress, and assigned subcontractors.
bullets.2: Subcontractor management — which subcontractor took on which scope, at what price, and how much has been paid, on one screen.
bullets.3: Progress-based payment tracking — payments are logged against the percentage of work actually completed.
bullets.4: Material in/out tracking — material delivered to site is tracked per project, similar to the stock/variant logic we built for FurCRM.
bullets.5: Role-based access — site manager, accounting, and management connect to the same system with different permissions.

construction-erp.painTitle: Where construction firms lose track of process

painPoints.1: When subcontractor payments are calculated by hand in a spreadsheet, the gap between completed work and amount paid surfaces too late.
painPoints.2: When material deliveries are logged in separate sheets per site, no one can see how much material a given project has actually consumed.
painPoints.3: When several projects run at once, which subcontractor is on which job lives only in the site manager's memory.

detail.1: Construction companies typically run several projects at once, each with its own subcontractor network, material flow, and payment schedule. When that complexity is managed in spreadsheets, information about how much of a scope a subcontractor has completed — and how much they've been paid against it — stays scattered; progress-payment calculations get delayed or miscalculated. Material tracking has the same problem: when deliveries are tied to a supplier rather than a project, no one can see how much material a given project has actually consumed. A construction ERP unifies these three data points — project, subcontractor, material — in one model, so management sees which project is straining budget early, not late.
detail.2: We don't have a construction-sector ERP delivered yet — we say that plainly. But the production tracking, dealer management, and accounts/finance modules we built for FurCRM in the furniture industry — tracking what stage a job is at and who owes what to whom — apply the same logic to subcontractor and progress-payment tracking. The stock and accounting integration we built into Ambalaj Cini's back-office is a direct reference for material in/out tracking too. We've already worked in construction on the web side — Velis LTD's corporate site — so we know the sector's terminology and workflow; what's missing is simply that this specific ERP hasn't been built before.
detail.3: We start by mapping how your company calculates progress payments and structures subcontractor agreements — we don't offer tax or contract-law advice here; we encode the calculation logic you define. Project, subcontractor, and material modules are built in sequence; existing spreadsheet data migrates into the new system. Scope depends on how many concurrent projects and how large your subcontractor network is; a small firm might need only project and payment tracking, while a larger one prioritizes material tracking and role-based access sooner. We test the system against real site data before handover.

construction-erp.ctaText: Get subcontractor and progress-payment tracking out of spreadsheets — let's talk about your construction ERP.

manufacturing-erp.title: ERP for Manufacturing Companies
manufacturing-erp.metaTitle: ERP for Manufacturing Companies | Piton Studios
manufacturing-erp.metaDescription: We build custom ERP systems unifying production, stock, order, and dealer tracking in one panel — the architecture we built for furniture with FurCRM.
manufacturing-erp.intro: A manufacturing ERP shows how much stock exists per product, what stage each order is at in production, and how much each dealer owes — all from one panel. We built exactly this for FurCRM, a furniture manufacturer: product/variant, accounts, quote-order-invoice flow, and dealer management unified in one system — the same architecture adapts to other manufacturing sectors.

bullets.1: Product- and variant-level stock tracking — how much of which model, in which color or size, is on one screen.
bullets.2: Production tracking panel — which stage an order is at in production, the same module we built for FurCRM.
bullets.3: Dealer management — dealer-specific pricing, order history, and account balance tracked from one place.
bullets.4: Quote-order-invoice flow moves forward automatically — the same data is never entered by hand three times.
bullets.5: Staff, commission, and performance modules report production efficiency from the same system.

manufacturing-erp.painTitle: Where manufacturers lose ground without an ERP

painPoints.1: When stock is tracked in spreadsheets, the gap between actual and recorded stock causes orders to be planned wrong.
painPoints.2: When dealer balances live in separate ledgers, figuring out who owes what becomes a manual exercise at month-end.
painPoints.3: When quotes, orders, and invoices are separate documents, the same information gets entered by hand three times, compounding error risk.

detail.1: In manufacturing, complexity mostly comes from product variety: dozens of variants of the same product, each with its own stock level, each order at its own production stage. Tracking this in spreadsheets works at a certain scale, but as product and dealer count grow, row count grows with it; which variant is out of stock or which dealer has an overdue balance gets noticed too late. A manufacturing ERP unifies this data in one schema: product/variant, order, production stage, and dealer account are linked — entering an order automatically updates stock, the production plan, and the dealer's balance, with nothing kept in sync by hand.
detail.2: The concrete proof of this approach is FurCRM: for furniture manufacturers we unified product & variant management, customer CRM, accounts & finance tracking, the quote-order-invoice flow, and dealer management in one panel; a production tracking screen, reporting dashboard, and staff/commission modules cover the entire operation. Built as our own product, this is our most complete example of sector-specific SaaS productization. We adapt the same data model — product/variant, order, production stage, dealer account — beyond furniture to other manufacturing sectors; the core architecture stays the same while field names and business rules change to fit yours.
detail.3: We start by mapping your product and variant structure, order process, and dealer network — the same process-audit and data-model-design steps we followed for FurCRM. Existing spreadsheet and accounting data migrates into the new system, and the team is trained before go-live. Scope depends on your product variety and dealer count; a smaller manufacturer might need only stock and order tracking, while a firm with a wide dealer network prioritizes the accounts/collections module sooner. The system is built on PostgreSQL so new modules can be added as you grow, whether that means a new dealer network or an additional production line.

manufacturing-erp.ctaText: Bring production and dealer tracking into one panel — let's talk about your manufacturing ERP.

b2b-dealer-portal.title: B2B Ordering Portal for Dealers
b2b-dealer-portal.metaTitle: B2B Ordering Portal for Dealers | Piton Studios
b2b-dealer-portal.metaDescription: We build B2B portals where each dealer orders at their own pricing, combining FurCRM's dealer management with the order/stock back-office from Ambalaj Cini.
b2b-dealer-portal.intro: A B2B dealer portal is the front end where each dealer logs in, orders at their own negotiated pricing, and sees their own order history and account balance. FurCRM's dealer management module already handles dealer-specific pricing and order tracking; Ambalaj Cini's order/stock/shipping back-office is a direct fit for the rest of this portal's infrastructure.

bullets.1: Dealer-specific price list — each dealer sees the price in their own agreement, not a generic list price.
bullets.2: Order history and reorder — a dealer repeats a past order in one click, no phone call or WhatsApp message needed.
bullets.3: Account balance visibility — dealers check their own balance in the portal instead of calling accounting.
bullets.4: Stock sync — the moment stock changes, it reflects on the dealer's screen instantly, the way we built it into Ambalaj Cini's back-office.
bullets.5: Role-based admin panel — the manufacturer manages which dealer sits at which price tier from one screen.

b2b-dealer-portal.painTitle: Where manual dealer ordering breaks down

painPoints.1: When orders come in by phone or WhatsApp, sales staff have to re-enter them by hand, adding room for error.
painPoints.2: When dealer-specific pricing lives in a spreadsheet, a new employee can quote the wrong price.
painPoints.3: When a dealer can't see their own balance, they call accounting every time, costing both sides time.

detail.1: The real complexity in B2B sales is that every dealer has a different price agreement, a different payment term, and their own ordering habits. When orders are taken by phone or email and entered by hand, that variation becomes error-prone — wrong pricing, a forgotten discount, a late entry. A B2B portal puts this process directly in the dealer's hands: they log in, see their own price, and place their own order; on the manufacturer's side, that order lands directly in stock and accounting, with no re-entry. This frees sales staff's time from taking orders toward developing new dealers.
detail.2: We've built the two core pieces of this portal separately and are ready to combine them: FurCRM's dealer management module runs dealer-specific pricing, orders, and account tracking in the furniture industry; Ambalaj Cini's back-office unifies stock, shipping, invoicing, and accounting in one panel, sending web push and email alerts to both customer and team the moment order status changes. We build the B2B dealer portal at the intersection of these two: a simple ordering interface for the dealer, and FurCRM's dealer-account logic plus Ambalaj Cini's stock/notification infrastructure on the manufacturer's side. We haven't yet combined these two into a single dealer portal — we say that plainly.
detail.3: We start by mapping your existing dealer agreements and price tiers, then build dealer login, ordering, stock visibility, and account balance modules in sequence. Payment can be integrated with a provider like PayTR or Stripe, or an order can simply post to the account balance and be collected the traditional way — we decide based on how you're used to collecting payment. Scope depends on your dealer count and how complex your pricing tiers are; a handful of large dealers might need only a simple order form, while a manufacturer with hundreds of dealers prioritizes automatic price tiers and reporting sooner.

b2b-dealer-portal.ctaText: Move dealer orders off the phone and WhatsApp and onto a portal — let's talk about your B2B portal.

restaurant-qr-ordering.title: QR Menu & Ordering for Restaurants
restaurant-qr-ordering.metaTitle: QR Menu & Ordering for Restaurants | Piton Studios
restaurant-qr-ordering.metaDescription: We build custom software for restaurants and cafes: table-side QR menu, direct ordering, and orders that land instantly on a kitchen screen — no paper tickets.
restaurant-qr-ordering.intro: A QR menu and ordering system lets a customer scan a code at their table, browse the menu, and place an order that lands instantly on a kitchen screen. We haven't delivered this exact flow for a restaurant yet; we adapt the order management from Boon Fresh and the real-time notification infrastructure from Ambalaj Cini to a restaurant's workflow.

bullets.1: Table-specific QR code — a customer opens their own table's menu, and the order is automatically tied to that table.
bullets.2: Direct ordering — the customer picks from the menu and places the order from their own phone, without waiting for a server.
bullets.3: Kitchen screen — an incoming order lands in the kitchen instantly, no paper ticket or verbal handoff needed.
bullets.4: Real-time status updates — similar to the web push infrastructure we built into Ambalaj Cini, the table gets notified the moment the order is ready.
bullets.5: Menu management panel — price changes or an item running out update instantly, so a customer never orders something that's gone.

restaurant-qr-ordering.painTitle: Where restaurants lose time in the ordering process

painPoints.1: When server headcount stays fixed during a rush, order-taking slows down and customers wait impatiently.
painPoints.2: When an order is written on paper and relayed verbally to the kitchen, items get misheard or dropped.
painPoints.3: When the menu changes, printed copies fall out of date and a customer tries to order something no longer sold.

detail.1: The bottleneck in a restaurant's ordering process is usually not staff but information flow: a customer's request travels to the server, the server's note travels to the kitchen verbally or on paper, and every handoff carries delay and error risk. A QR menu and ordering system removes these intermediate steps — the customer enters the order directly into the system, which drops it onto the kitchen screen instantly. This doesn't just add speed; order capacity increases even with fixed staffing during a rush, because the time spent taking orders shifts to serving customers. On the menu side, an item that's run out can be pulled instantly, so no one tries to order something that no longer exists.
detail.2: We've built the pieces of this system separately in different projects: at Boon Fresh we built order management and tracking for a fresh-food delivery platform; in Ambalaj Cini's back-office we built infrastructure that sends real-time web push and email alerts to both customer and team the moment an order, payment, or stock status changes. A QR menu and kitchen screen is these two translated into restaurant terms: order management follows Boon Fresh's logic, real-time notification follows Ambalaj Cini's push infrastructure. We haven't yet combined this end-to-end in a restaurant project — we say that plainly, describing what we'd build rather than claiming delivery.
detail.3: We start by mapping the kitchen's actual workflow — table count, menu category count, which screen or device the kitchen will use. The customer side is built as a mobile web interface with no app download required; the kitchen screen is a separate view running on a tablet or fixed display. Whether payment is taken at the table or at the register changes the flow — we decide that together up front. Scope depends on table count and menu complexity; a small cafe might need just a simple QR menu, while a busy restaurant prioritizes a kitchen screen and stock-based menu updates sooner.
