transfer-driver-app.metaDescription: We build driver apps for transfer companies: job assignment, route view, status updates; no native app published yet — we decide PWA vs. native together.
transfer-driver-app.intro: A driver app is the mobile tool a dispatcher uses to assign a job to a driver, the driver uses to see the route, and both use to track status — on the way, completed. We haven't published a native app yet; we bring the reservation experience built across five transfer sites and our PWA/native decision process to this app.

bullets.1: Job assignment screen — dispatch assigns an incoming booking to an available driver with one tap.
bullets.2: Route view — the driver sees customer location and route information in the app, without switching to a separate maps app.
bullets.3: Status updates — on the way, with customer, completed states are logged with one tap, visible to dispatch instantly.
bullets.4: PWA-or-native decision — if you don't genuinely need hardware access like camera or Bluetooth, a PWA can be faster and cheaper.
bullets.5: Integration with the dispatch panel — the driver app is designed as an extension of the reservation flow we've built across five projects, not a separate system.

transfer-driver-app.painTitle: Where transfer companies lose ground coordinating drivers

painPoints.1: When job assignment happens by phone or WhatsApp, dispatch tracks driver availability from memory.
painPoints.2: When no one knows where a driver is or what stage a job is at, the customer calls dispatch and dispatch calls the driver.
painPoints.3: When end-of-shift reporting is done by hand, tallying how many jobs each driver completed becomes a month-end scramble.

detail.1: At transfer and taxi companies, coordination between dispatch and drivers usually runs over phone and WhatsApp; this becomes a bottleneck once volume picks up — dispatch tracks driver availability from memory, and drivers learn job details verbally. A driver app turns this coordination into a structured flow: a job goes directly from dispatch to the driver, the driver sees route and customer information in the app, and updates status with one tap. On dispatch's side, which driver is on which job becomes visible instantly; end-of-shift reporting stops being a manual reconstruction and comes out of the system automatically.
detail.2: We haven't published a native mobile app yet — we say that plainly. But the reservation flow we built for Jet Transfer Cyprus, Aydın Transfer, Kıbrıs Lefkoşa Taksi, Kardeşler Taxi, and Welcome Pickups gave us deep knowledge of this sector's business model — routes, pricing, customer communication; what's missing is simply carrying that knowledge to the driver's side, in a mobile interface. Our mobile-app service starts by deciding between native and PWA: if you don't need hardware access like camera or Bluetooth, a PWA — single codebase, no store review — is usually faster and cheaper; if native is genuinely required, we ship from one React Native/Expo codebase to both stores.
detail.3: We start by mapping dispatch's job-assignment process and drivers' actual working patterns — how many drivers, how many concurrent jobs, what information they need. We then build the dispatch panel and driver app on the same data model, as an extension of our existing reservation system rather than a separate one. If native is required, App Store and Google Play accounts open in your name, and we handle store review and release. Scope depends on fleet size and daily job volume; a small fleet might need only a simple status-update screen, while a larger fleet prioritizes real-time location tracking sooner.

transfer-driver-app.ctaText: Move driver coordination off the phone and WhatsApp and into an app — let's talk about your mobile app.

ecommerce-meta-ads.title: Meta Ads for E-commerce
ecommerce-meta-ads.metaTitle: Meta Ads for E-commerce | Piton Studios
ecommerce-meta-ads.metaDescription: We run catalog and dynamic-retargeting Facebook/Instagram campaigns for online stores — part of the Google Ads plus Meta effort that grew Ambalaj Cini by 30%.
ecommerce-meta-ads.intro: Meta ads for e-commerce turn your product catalog into automatic Facebook and Instagram ads and re-target visitors who leave your site without buying, with the exact product they looked at. At Ambalaj Cini, the Meta ads we ran alongside Google Ads campaigns were part of the effort that grew the business by 30%.

bullets.1: Catalog ads — your product feed connects to Meta so the entire catalog turns into ads automatically, instead of designing each one by hand.
bullets.2: Dynamic retargeting — a shopper who adds an item to cart and leaves sees an ad for that exact product.
bullets.3: Meta Pixel and Conversions API set up together — conversion data doesn't depend on browser trackers.
bullets.4: Lookalike audiences — reach new users who resemble your existing customer profile, avoiding broad, unfocused targeting.
bullets.5: Weekly reporting centers on ROAS and revenue, not impressions or likes.

ecommerce-meta-ads.painTitle: Where Meta ads go wrong for e-commerce stores

painPoints.1: Without the catalog connected to Meta, every product needs its own manually designed ad, so only a fraction of the catalog ever gets advertised.
painPoints.2: Without Pixel or Conversions API set up correctly, no one can see which ad actually drove a sale, so budget gets allocated by guesswork.
painPoints.3: Without retargeting a cart abandoner, the shopper closest to buying never gets shown the ad again.

detail.1: In e-commerce, the value of Meta ads scales directly with catalog size: instead of advertising hundreds of products one by one, a product feed connects to Meta and the system decides what to show whom based on behavior. For this to work, measurement has to be set up correctly first — no budget should go out before Meta Pixel and server-side Conversions API are both in place, or which ad actually drove a sale will look incomplete because of browser trackers. Once that foundation is set, catalog ads and dynamic retargeting directly move conversion rate by calling a cart-abandoning shopper back with the exact product they saw.
detail.2: The concrete proof of this approach is Ambalaj Cini: alongside the e-commerce platform we built, we designed and ran Google Ads and Facebook (Meta) campaigns together, and the resulting growth effort delivered a 30% increase — a number we attribute to Google Ads and Meta working together, not to Meta alone. In our Meta ads service, we always set up Pixel and Conversions API before any campaign; campaign architecture is split into awareness, consideration, and conversion stages, each with its own budget and goal. Listed as a Meta Partner for this service, we report on revenue and ROAS, not likes or reach.
detail.3: We start by auditing your existing account and any measurement infrastructure; if Pixel/Conversions API is missing or misconfigured, we fix that before building anything new on top of broken data. For catalog ads we prepare the product feed, and dynamic retargeting segments — cart abandoners, product viewers, past customers — are built separately. For the first two weeks we don't make major changes, giving the algorithm room to learn; after that, a weekly optimization cycle shifts budget toward whichever segment converts best. Our management fee is separate from ad spend — you pay Meta directly for that.

ecommerce-meta-ads.ctaText: Turn your catalog into automatic Meta ads — let's talk about Meta ads management for your store.
